biography: Jason Keats, a name synonymous with audacious overtakes and, occasionally, spectacular crashes, hails from the icy plains of Manitoba, Canada. Unlike most racers who grew up karting, Jason's first taste of speed came on frozen lakes, modifying snowmobiles with his mechanic father. This unconventional training instilled in him a raw, instinctive feel for vehicle dynamics. His transition to circuit racing was late, but impactful. A defining moment came during his rookie season in the North American Touring Car Championship; downshifting a gear too early at Mosport, he spun violently, collecting three cars in a cloud of tire smoke. While disastrous, the sheer audacity of the move – attempting to pass three cars into Moss Corner – caught the eye of Grigio Nimbus team owner, Enzo Bellissima, who saw untapped potential beneath the recklessness. Now, a veteran in his late 30s, Keats is still with Grigio Nimbus, balancing his natural aggression with a hard-won maturity, chasing that elusive championship title that has always seemed just out of reach.
drivingStyle: Keats drives with a flair bordering on recklessness. He's an opportunist, always searching for the smallest gap, often attempting passes where others wouldn't dare. His corner entry speeds are notoriously high, pushing the limits of grip and occasionally exceeding them. While this approach makes him exciting to watch, it also leads to inconsistent results. Tire management isn't his forte; he tends to overdrive the car early in the stint, sacrificing long-run pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, he can either deliver a stunning performance or crumble spectacularly, depending on the phase of the moon, apparently.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision at Circuit Gilles Villeneuve that cost Dubois the championship. She publicly accuses Keats of deliberately taking her out.

rivalries.name: Marco Vitale
rivalries.reason: A battle of egos and driving styles. Vitale, known for his precise, calculated approach, often criticizes Keats's aggressive tactics, leading to heated exchanges in press conferences.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: Tanaka, a rising star, represents the new generation of racers, and Keats sees him as a threat to his relevance. Keats has been known to make aggressive moves on track against Tanaka, trying to 'teach him a lesson'.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of maple leaf-patterned socks for every race.
Insists on personally polishing his helmet visor before each session, believing it improves his vision.
Listens to a specific playlist of 80s power ballads on repeat in the garage before qualifying, claiming it 'gets his blood pumping'.
famousQuote: "You're not racing if you're not on the edge. And sometimes, the edge bites back."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2018 with Grigio Nimbus, despite starting from the back of the grid after a pre-race engine change. Keats drove a heroic triple stint in the early morning hours, making up significant ground and setting the stage for his teammates to secure the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Canadian Grand Prix in 2021. Under immense pressure from Dubois, he locked up his brakes entering the final chicane, handing the victory to his rival and sending the home crowd into stunned silence.
